thread:
anya: Heads up — after today's UX rollout I'm seeing the dashboard charts stutter on first paint. Sparklines take ~2.5s to render, full heatmap 4-5s. Happening in canary and prod for a subset of users. :frowning:

sam: Repro? browser / network / corp VPN?

anya: Chrome on macOS, corp VPN off. CPU looks fine. Network waterfall: initial bundle ~800ms then a ~1.5s gap, then lots of small requests. KV cache hit rate for the sparkline prefix is low (~22%). Telemetry shows spike in kvcache_miss for route /console/metrics/chart-route.

lia: Did the prefetch priority change land in that rollout? We lowered prefetch priority for non-essential widgets in last PR.

matt: Yep — routing/prefetch policy was updated yesterday: prefetches go into quota group `ui-prefetch-low` and we throttle when quota > 80%. If quota enforcement flipped, prefetch requests get deprioritized.

anya: I can repro locally by forcing the header to low. Quick repro snippet: 
```http
GET /api/metrics/sparkline?range=1h
x-prefetch-priority: low
x-kv-lookup: prefix
```

sam: Can we check the prefetch quota meter for us-west?

ops-bot: quota-meter update: ui-prefetch quota at 87% (us-west-2) at 15:12 UTC.

sam: OK that explains the behavior. When quota > threshold we downgrade prefetches and then routing policy pushes those requests to cheaper/compat model instances — cold KV reads + slower kernels = double latency hit.

lia: Telemetry shows the fallback variant has a much higher cold-start latency for KV-backed charts. Combined with prefix cache misses, explains the 3-4s LCP.

matt: Short term options: revert the prefetch priority flip, increase quota threshold, or pin charts to high-priority prefetch. Long term: ensure prefetch-critical path gets either dedicated pool or warm KV cache and record the prefetch-priority header in traces.

anya: Can we patch canary to force prefetch priority=high for chart widgets only? e.g., flag `ui.prefetch.priority.charts=high`.

sam: I'll prepare a canary patch and run it in 15m.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary/ui/patch-prefetch-charts (build 232)

lia: Also please add a telemetry alert: if median chart first-paint > 1.2s for `chart-route` -> page-freeze paging alert and page owner ping.

matt: Added an eval set in Redwood Optimize for chart rendering so we can detect regressions and get quantization/model advice sooner.

anya: Canary patch results: sparkline LCP down to ~450ms, heatmap first paint ~900ms. kvcache hit rate for prefix jumped back to 68% on canary.

sam: Let's roll to prod at 5% for 30m, monitor kvcache hit, prefetch quota, and LCP. Abort criteria: kvcache hit < 50% OR median LCP > 1s.

matt: Logging note: let's attach `route=chart-route` and `x-prefetch-priority` as indexed fields in telemetry events — makes correlation trivial.

anya: Thanks — follow-up PR with the flag and tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/982 (contains canary config + telemetry tags)

deploy-bot: Canary rolled to 5% -> success.

ops-bot: Alert suppression auto-acknowledged. :thumbsup:
